reasoning_traces.think:
The lead scoring system models a discrete-time Markov chain where each state represents a lead's readiness level (Pass, Cool, Warm, Hot). Each primitive contributes a scalar value to a composite score. Spatial coverage adds fixed gain if within service area. Engagement strength reflects active interest via web signals. Content frequency penalizes non-local or non-traditional businesses. These scores form a vector in R^3 which maps to a categorical state via thresholding. The system exhibits duality between high- and low-engagement leads, with failure modes including misclassification due to noisy signals or geographic ambiguity. Temporal dynamics are implicit in the sequence logic: 'sequence, don't pitch twice' implies state transitions must be delayed or conditional.
